title: Compiling-Away of Unmarked Accesses
pattern: Reading a plain non-atomic shared variable in a tight loop to wait for a state transition.
why_bad: Since the compiler assumes single-threaded execution for plain variables, it detects that `stop_flag` is not modified within the loop body. It optimizes the code by loading the variable once into a register, transforming the loop into an infinite loop if `stop_flag` was initially zero.
detection: A loop condition reading a plain, non-volatile, non-atomic variable that is modified concurrently by other threads.
counterexample: The variable is explicitly marked `volatile` or read using marked primitives like `READ_ONCE()`.
source: Paul McKenney Appendix C.3, Appendix E.15
